sanskrit: budhyāmi tvāṃ vṛtrahaṇaṃ śatakratuṃ; vyatikramantaṃ bhuvanāni viśvā kaccin na vācā vṛjinaṃ kadā cid; akārṣaṃ te manaso 'bhiṣaṅgāt
english: I recognize you now as the slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of a hundred sacrifices, who ranges across all the worlds. I trust that I have never, through some seizure of the mind, spoken a single crooked word against you.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca yasmād imaṃ lokapathaṃ prajānām; anvāgamaṃ padavāde gajasya tasmād bhavān praṇataṃ mānuśāstu; bravīṣi yat tat karavāṇi sarvam
english: Śakra said: Since, on the pretext of this elephant, I have drawn you along the path that creatures travel to the worlds, instruct me, who bow before you; whatever you command, all of it I shall do.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca śvetaṃ kareṇuṃ mama putranāgaṃ; yaṃ me 'hārṣīr daśavarṣāṇi bālam yo me vane vasato 'bhūd dvitīyas; tam eva me dehi surendra nāgam
english: Gautama said: My elephant-son, the white-tusked creature you bore away from me when he was but ten years a calf, who was a second self to me as I dwelt in the forest — that very elephant restore to me, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca ayaṃ sutas te dvijamukhya nāgaś; cāghrāyate tvām abhivīkṣamāṇaḥ pādau ca te nāsikayopajighrate; śreyo mama dhyāhi namaś ca te 'stu
english: Śakra said: Here is your son, O foremost of the twice-born — the elephant who breathes you in as he gazes upon you, who sniffs at your feet with his trunk. Wish well for me, and may homage be yours.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca śivaṃ sadaiveha surendra tubhyaṃ; dhyāyāmi pūjāṃ ca sadā prayuñje mamāpi tvaṃ śakra śivaṃ dadasva; tvayā dattaṃ pratigṛhṇāmi nāgam
english: Gautama said: Always do I wish you well here, O lord of the gods, and ever do I offer you worship. To me too, O Śakra, grant your blessing; the elephant given by you I gladly receive.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca yeṣāṃ vedā nihitā vai guhāyāṃ; manīṣiṇāṃ sattvavatāṃ mahātmanām teṣāṃ tvayaikena mahātmanāsmi; buddhas tasmāt prītimāṃs te 'ham adya
english: Śakra said: Among those wise and steadfast great-souled ones in whose secret heart the Vedas lie hidden, by you alone, great soul, have I been truly understood; and so today I am well pleased with you.

sanskrit: hantaihi brāhmaṇa kṣipraṃ saha putreṇa hastinā prāpnuhi tvaṃ śubhāṃl lokān ahnāya ca cirāya ca
english: Come then, brāhmaṇa, come quickly, together with your son the elephant, and attain the auspicious worlds, both for the present and for all time to come.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa gautamaṃ puraskṛtya saha putreṇa hastinā divam ācakrame vajrī sadbhiḥ saha durāsadam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the wielder of the thunderbolt, setting Gautama before him along with his son the elephant, ascended with the holy ones to heaven, that realm so hard to reach.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dānaṃ bahuvidhākāraṃ śāntiḥ satyam ahiṃsatā svadāratuṣṭiś coktā te phalaṃ dānasya caiva yat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have spoken of giving in its many forms, of peace, truth, and non-injury, of contentment with one's own wife, and of the fruit that giving bears.

sanskrit: pitāmahasya viditaṃ kim anyatra tapobalāt tapaso yat paraṃ te 'dya tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: What is known to grandsire that is greater than the power of austerity? If there is anything beyond austerity, you ought to explain it to me today.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tapaḥ pracakṣate yāvat tāval lokā yudhiṣṭhira mataṃ mama tu kaunteya tapo nānaśanāt param
english: Bhīṣma said: As far as men declare austerity to reach, so far do the worlds extend, Yudhiṣṭhira; but my view, son of Kuntī, is that no austerity surpasses fasting.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bhagīrathasya saṃvādaṃ brahmaṇaś ca mahātmanaḥ
english: On this point too they recite an ancient tale: the dialogue of Bhagīratha and the great-souled Brahmā.

sanskrit: atītya suralokaṃ ca gavāṃ lokaṃ ca bhārata ṛṣilokaṃ ca so 'gacchad bhagīratha iti śrutiḥ
english: Having passed beyond the world of the gods, the world of the cattle, O Bhārata, and the world of the seers, Bhagīratha went onward — so runs the tradition.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa vacaḥ prāha brahmā rājan bhagīratham kathaṃ bhagīrathāgās tvam imaṃ deśaṃ durāsadam
english: Seeing him, Brahmā spoke these words to Bhagīratha, O king: How is it, Bhagīratha, that you have come to this region so hard to reach?

sanskrit: na hi devā na gandharvā na manuṣyā bhagīratha āyānty ataptatapasaḥ kathaṃ vai tvam ihāgataḥ
english: For neither gods nor gandharvas nor men come here, Bhagīratha, if they have not performed austerities. How then have you come to this place?

sanskrit: bhagīratha uvāca niḥśaṅkam annam adadaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ; śataṃ sahasrāṇi sadaiva dānam brāhmaṃ vrataṃ nityam āsthāya viddhi; na tv evāhaṃ tasya phalād ihāgām
english: Bhagīratha said: Without misgiving I gave food to the brāhmaṇas — a hundred thousand gifts, always and unceasingly — ever holding to the sacred brahminical vow; yet know that it was not by the fruit of this that I came here.

sanskrit: daśaikarātrān daśa pañcarātrān; ekādaśaikādaśakān kratūṃś ca jyotiṣṭomānāṃ ca śataṃ yad iṣṭaṃ; phalena tenāpi ca nāgato 'ham
english: Ten single-night rites, ten five-night rites, eleven elevenfold sacrifices, and a hundred Jyotiṣṭoma offerings I performed; yet not even by the fruit of these have I come here.

sanskrit: yac cāvasaṃ jāhnavītīranityaḥ; śataṃ samās tapyamānas tapo 'ham adāṃ ca tatrāśvatarīsahasraṃ; nārīpuraṃ na ca tenāham āgām
english: And though I dwelt ever on the bank of the Jāhnavī, practicing austerity for a hundred years, and there gave a thousand she-mules and a city full of women, not even by that have I come here.

sanskrit: daśāyutāni cāśvānām ayutāni ca viṃśatim puṣkareṣu dvijātibhyaḥ prādāṃ gāś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: A hundred thousand horses, and twenty times ten thousand more, I gave at Puṣkara to the twice-born, and cattle by the thousands.

sanskrit: suvarṇacandroḍupadhāriṇīnāṃ; kanyottamānām adadaṃ sragviṇīnām ṣaṣṭiṃ sahasrāṇi vibhūṣitānāṃ; jāmbūnadair ābharaṇair na tena
english: Sixty thousand maidens of the finest sort, adorned with garlands and bearing golden ornaments shaped like moon and star, decked in jewelry of pure river-gold, I gave away — yet not by that did I come.

sanskrit: daśārbudāny adadaṃ gosavejyāsv; ekaikaśo daśa gā lokanātha samānavatsāḥ payasā samanvitāḥ; suvarṇakāṃsyopaduhā na tena
english: At the Gosava sacrifices I gave a hundred million cattle, ten at a time, O lord of the worlds — each with its calf and rich in milk, milked into vessels of gold and bronze — yet not by that did I come.

sanskrit: aptoryāmeṣu niyatam ekaikasmin daśādadam gṛṣṭīnāṃ kṣīradātrīṇāṃ rohiṇīnāṃ na tena ca
english: At each of the Aptoryāma rites I duly gave ten young red cows that gave plentiful milk — yet not even by that did I come here.

sanskrit: dogdhrīṇāṃ vai gavāṃ caiva prayutāni daśaiva ha prādāṃ daśaguṇaṃ brahman na ca tenāham āgataḥ
english: Of milch cows I gave ten million, and ten times that again, O Brahmā — yet not by that have I come here.

sanskrit: vājināṃ bāhlijātānām ayutāny adadaṃ daśa karkāṇāṃ hemamālānāṃ na ca tenāham āgataḥ
english: Of horses born in Bāhli, white steeds wearing golden chains, I gave a hundred thousand — yet not by that have I come here.

sanskrit: koṭīś ca kāñcanasyāṣṭau prādāṃ brahman daśa tv aham ekaikasmin kratau tena phalenāhaṃ na cāgataḥ
english: Eighty million pieces of gold, ten times over, I gave, O Brahmā — at each single sacrifice — yet not by that fruit have I come here.

sanskrit: vājināṃ śyāmakarṇānāṃ haritānāṃ pitāmaha prādāṃ hemasrajāṃ brahman koṭīr daśa ca sapta ca
english: Of tawny horses with dark ears, bearing golden garlands, O grandsire, I gave seventeen times ten million, O Brahmā.

sanskrit: īṣādantān mahākāyān kāñcanasragvibhūṣitān patnīmataḥ sahasrāṇi prāyacchaṃ daśa sapta ca
english: Mighty-bodied elephants with tusks like chariot-poles, decked with golden garlands and accompanied by their mates — these I gave, seventeen thousand of them.

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtānāṃ deveśa divyaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ rathānāṃ kāñcanāṅgānāṃ sahasrāṇy adadaṃ daśa sapta cānyāni yuktāni vājibhiḥ samalaṃkṛtaiḥ
english: Chariots with golden frames, adorned with divine ornaments of gold, O lord of the gods, I gave away — seventeen thousand of them — and others besides, yoked to richly caparisoned horses.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāvayavāḥ ke cid vedair ye saṃprakīrtitāḥ vājapeyeṣu daśasu prādāṃ tenāpi nāpy aham
english: Whatever portions of sacrificial fee are extolled in the Vedas, at ten Vājapeya rites I bestowed them all — yet not even by that did I come here.

sanskrit: śakratulyaprabhāvānām ijyayā vikrameṇa ca sahasraṃ niṣkakaṇṭhānām adadaṃ dakṣiṇām aham
english: As sacrificial fee I gave a thousand men equal to Śakra in their power of sacrifice and in valor, all wearing golden necklaces.

sanskrit: vijitya nṛpatīn sarvān makhair iṣṭvā pitāmaha aṣṭabhyo rājasūyebhyo na ca tenāham āgataḥ
english: Having conquered all kings and offered sacrifices, O grandsire, even by eight Rājasūya rites I did not come here by that means.

sanskrit: srotaś ca yāvad gaṅgāyāś channam āsīj jagatpate dakṣiṇābhiḥ pravṛttābhir mama nāgāṃ ca tatkṛte
english: And though the whole stream of the Gaṅgā was overspread, O lord of the world, by the sacrificial gifts that flowed from my hands, not for the sake of that did I come.

sanskrit: vājināṃ ca sahasre dve suvarṇaśatabhūṣite varaṃ grāmaśataṃ cāham ekaikasya tridhādadam tapasvī niyatāhāraḥ śamam āsthāya vāgyataḥ
english: Two thousand horses adorned with a hundred ornaments of gold, and a hundred choice villages for each man, I gave threefold — an ascetic of measured food, abiding in calm and curbed in speech.

sanskrit: dīrghakālaṃ himavati gaṅgāyāś ca durutsahām mūrdhnā dhārāṃ mahādevaḥ śirasā yām adhārayat na tenāpy aham āgacchaṃ phaleneha pitāmaha
english: For a long age in the Himālaya I dwelt, by whose unbearable torrent of the Gaṅgā — the stream that Mahādeva once bore upon his head — yet not even by that fruit did I come here, O grandsire.

sanskrit: śamyākṣepair ayajaṃ yac ca devān; sadyaskānām ayutaiś cāpi yat tat trayodaśadvādaśāhāṃś ca deva; sapauṇḍarīkān na ca teṣāṃ phalena
english: With sacrifices measured by the cast of the yoke-pin I worshiped the gods, and with ten thousand one-day rites, and thirteen- and twelve-day offerings, O god, together with the Pauṇḍarīka — yet not by the fruit of these did I come.

sanskrit: aṣṭau sahasrāṇi kakudminām ahaṃ; śuklarṣabhāṇām adadaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ ekaikaṃ vai kāñcanaṃ śṛṅgam ebhyaḥ; patnīś caiṣām adadaṃ niṣkakaṇṭhīḥ
english: Eight thousand humped white bulls I gave to the brāhmaṇas, each with a single horn cased in gold, and along with them their cows wearing golden necklaces.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaratnanicitān adadaṃ ratnaparvatān dhanadhānyasamṛddhāṃś ca grāmāñ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Mountains of jewels heaped with gold and gems I gave, and villages rich in wealth and grain, by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: śataṃ śatānāṃ gṛṣṭīnām adadaṃ cāpy atandritaḥ iṣṭvānekair mahāyajñair brāhmaṇebhyo na tena ca
english: Ten thousand young cows I gave, unwearied, and offered many great sacrifices for the brāhmaṇas — yet not by that did I come here.

sanskrit: ekādaśāhair ayajaṃ sadakṣiṇair; dvirdvādaśāhair aśvamedhaiś ca deva ārkāyaṇaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiś ca brahmaṃs; teṣāṃ phaleneha na cāgato 'smi
english: With eleven-day rites attended by gifts, with twice-twelve-day rites and horse-sacrifices, O god, and with sixteen Ārkāyaṇa offerings, O Brahmā — yet not by the fruit of these have I come here.

sanskrit: niṣkaikakaṇṭham adadaṃ yojanāyataṃ; tad vistīrṇaṃ kāñcanapādapānām vanaṃ cūtānāṃ ratnavibhūṣitānāṃ; na caiva teṣām āgato 'haṃ phalena
english: I gave away a whole forest of golden trees, a league in length and breadth — a grove of mango trees adorned with jewels, each bearing a single golden trunk — yet not by the fruit of these have I come.

sanskrit: turāyaṇaṃ hi vratam apradhṛṣyam; akrodhano 'karavaṃ triṃśato 'bdān śataṃ gavām aṣṭa śatāni caiva; dine dine hy adadaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ
english: The unassailable Turāyaṇa vow, free of anger, I kept for thirty years; eight hundred and one cows, day after day, I gave to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: payasvinīnām atha rohiṇīnāṃ; tathaiva cāpy anaḍuhāṃ lokanātha prādāṃ nityaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sureśa; nehāgatas tena phalena cāham
english: Milch cows, red cows, and likewise draft-oxen, O lord of the worlds, I gave continually to the brāhmaṇas, O lord of the gods — yet not by that fruit have I come here.

sanskrit: triṃśad agnim ahaṃ brahmann ayajaṃ yac ca nityadā aṣṭābhiḥ sarvamedhaiś ca naramedhaiś ca saptabhiḥ
english: For thirty years, O Brahmā, I daily tended the sacred fire and worshiped with eight Sarvamedha rites and seven Naramedha rites.

sanskrit: daśabhir viśvajidbhiś ca śatair aṣṭādaśottaraiḥ na caiva teṣāṃ deveśa phalenāham ihāgataḥ
english: And with ten Viśvajit rites, and with a hundred and eighteen others — yet not by the fruit of these, O lord of the gods, have I come here.

sanskrit: sarayvāṃ bāhudāyāṃ ca gaṅgāyām atha naimiṣe gavāṃ śatānām ayutam adadaṃ na ca tena vai
english: On the Sarayū, the Bāhudā, the Gaṅgā, and at Naimiṣa I gave a million cattle — yet not by that did I come.

sanskrit: indreṇa guhyaṃ nihitaṃ vai guhāyāṃ; yad bhārgavas tapasehābhyavindat jājvalyamānam uśanastejaseha; tat sādhayām āsa mahaṃ vareṇyam
english: That secret hidden by Indra in a cave, which Bhārgava found here through austerity — blazing here with the splendor of Uśanas — that most excellent and great rite I brought to fulfillment.

sanskrit: tato me brāhmaṇās tuṣṭās tasmin karmaṇi sādhite sahasram ṛṣayaś cāsan ye vai tatra samāgatāḥ uktas tair asmi gaccha tvaṃ brahmalokam iti prabho
english: Then, when that rite was accomplished, the brāhmaṇas were pleased with me; a thousand seers were there assembled, and by them I was told: Go now to the world of Brahmā, O lord.

sanskrit: prītenoktaḥ sahasreṇa brāhmaṇānām ahaṃ prabho imaṃ lokam anuprāpto mā bhūt te 'tra vicāraṇā
english: Thus addressed by a thousand well-pleased brāhmaṇas, O lord, I have reached this world. Let there be no doubt in you upon this point.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ yathāvad vihitaṃ vidhātrā; pṛṣṭena vācyaṃ tu mayā yathāvat tapo hi nānyac cānaśanān mataṃ me; namo 'stu te devavara prasīda
english: As the Ordainer has duly fixed, so, being asked, must I speak duly; for I hold no austerity other than fasting. Homage be to you, O best of the gods — be gracious.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktavantaṃ taṃ brahmā rājānaṃ sma bhagīratham pūjayām āsa pūjārhaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Bhīṣma said: When King Bhagīratha had spoken thus, Brahmā honored him — worthy of honor as he was — with the rite ordained by sacred law.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śatāyur uktaḥ puruṣaḥ śatavīryaś ca vaidike kasmān mriyante puruṣā bālā api pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In the Vedic teaching man is said to have a span of a hundred years and the strength of a hundred. Why then, grandsire, do men die, even as children?

sanskrit: āyuṣmān kena bhavati svalpāyur vāpi mānavaḥ kena vā labhate kīrtiṃ kena vā labhate śriyam
english: By what does a man become long-lived, and by what short-lived? By what does he win renown, and by what does he gain prosperity?

sanskrit: tapasā brahmacaryeṇa japair homais tathauṣadhaiḥ janmanā yadi vācārāt tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Is it by austerity, by chastity, by silent prayer, by oblations, or by herbs; by birth, or rather by conduct? Tell me this, grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi yan māṃ tvam anupṛcchasi alpāyur yena bhavati dīrghāyur vāpi mānavaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall instruct you in what you ask of me — by what a man becomes short-lived or long-lived.

sanskrit: yena vā labhate kīrtiṃ yena vā labhate śriyam yathā ca vartan puruṣaḥ śreyasā saṃprayujyate
english: And by what he wins renown, and by what he gains prosperity, and how, by conducting himself rightly, a man becomes joined to the good.

sanskrit: ācārāl labhate hy āyur ācārāl labhate śriyam ācārāt kīrtim āpnoti puruṣaḥ pretya ceha ca
english: For it is from right conduct that a man gains long life, from conduct that he gains prosperity, and from conduct that he wins renown, both here and in the world hereafter.

sanskrit: durācāro hi puruṣo nehāyur vindate mahat trasanti yasmād bhūtāni tathā paribhavanti ca
english: For a man of evil conduct does not attain a great span of life here; creatures shrink from him, and likewise they hold him in contempt.

sanskrit: tasmāt kuryād ihācāraṃ ya icched bhūtim ātmanaḥ api pāpaśarīrasya ācāro hanty alakṣaṇam
english: Therefore let one who desires his own welfare practice right conduct in this world; even in one whose body bears the marks of sin, good conduct destroys the inauspicious sign.

sanskrit: ācāralakṣaṇo dharmaḥ santaś cācāralakṣaṇāḥ sādhūnāṃ ca yathā vṛttam etad ācāralakṣaṇam
english: Dharma has conduct for its mark, and the good are known by their conduct; and whatever is the way of the virtuous, that is the very mark of good conduct.

sanskrit: apy adṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vāpi puruṣaṃ dharmacāriṇam bhūtikarmāṇi kurvāṇaṃ taṃ janāḥ kurvate priyam
english: Even a man unseen or only heard of, if he walks in dharma and performs works of welfare, him people hold dear.

sanskrit: ye nāstikā niṣkriyāś ca guruśāstrātilaṅghinaḥ adharmajñā durācārās te bhavanti gatāyuṣaḥ
english: Those who are deniers and idle, who transgress teacher and scripture, who know not dharma and are evil in conduct — these become short of life.

sanskrit: viśīlā bhinnamaryādā nityaṃ saṃkīrṇamaithunāḥ alpāyuṣo bhavantīha narā nirayagāminaḥ
english: Men of bad character, who break all bounds and are forever promiscuous in their unions, become short-lived here and travelers to hell.

sanskrit: sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi samudācāravān naraḥ śraddadhāno 'nasūyaś ca śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati
english: Even a man lacking every auspicious mark, if he is well-conducted, full of faith, and free of envy, lives a hundred years.

sanskrit: akrodhanaḥ satyavādī bhūtānām avihiṃsakaḥ anasūyur ajihmaś ca śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati
english: Free of anger, speaking the truth, harming no creature, free of envy and of guile — such a man lives a hundred years.

sanskrit: loṣṭamardī tṛṇacchedī nakhakhādī ca yo naraḥ nityocchiṣṭaḥ saṃkusuko nehāyur vindate mahat
english: The man who crumbles clods, snaps off blades of grass, gnaws his nails, who is forever unclean from leavings and restless in his ways — he does not attain a great span of life here.

sanskrit: brāhme muhūrte budhyeta dharmārthau cānucintayet utthāyācamya tiṣṭheta pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Let him wake in the hour sacred to Brahmā and reflect upon dharma and worldly good; rising and sipping water, let him stand with joined palms through the morning twilight devotion.

sanskrit: evam evāparāṃ saṃdhyāṃ samupāsīta vāgyataḥ nekṣetādityam udyantaṃ nāstaṃ yāntaṃ kadā cana
english: In the very same way let him attend the evening twilight devotion with curbed speech; let him never gaze upon the sun as it rises or as it sets.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo dīrghasaṃdhyatvād dīrgham āyur avāpnuvan tasmāt tiṣṭhet sadā pūrvāṃ paścimāṃ caiva vāgyataḥ
english: The seers, through their long twilight devotions, won long life; therefore let one always stand, with curbed speech, through both the morning and the evening twilight.

sanskrit: ye ca pūrvām upāsante dvijāḥ saṃdhyāṃ na paścimām sarvāṃs tān dhārmiko rājā śūdrakarmāṇi kārayet
english: Those twice-born who attend the morning twilight but not the evening — all such men a righteous king should set to the labors of a śūdra.

sanskrit: paradārā na gantavyāḥ sarvavarṇeṣu karhi cit na hīdṛśam anāyuṣyaṃ loke kiṃ cana vidyate yādṛśaṃ puruṣasyeha paradāropasevanam
english: The wives of others must never be approached, in any of the four orders; for nothing in the world so shortens a man's life as the resorting to another's wife.

sanskrit: prasādhanaṃ ca keśānām añjanaṃ dantadhāvanam pūrvāhṇa eva kurvīta devatānāṃ ca pūjanam
english: The dressing of the hair, the anointing of the eyes, the cleaning of the teeth, and the worship of the gods — these let him perform in the early part of the day.

sanskrit: purīṣamūtre nodīkṣen nādhitiṣṭhet kadā cana udakyayā ca saṃbhāṣāṃ na kurvīta kadā cana
english: Let him never look upon dung or urine, nor ever tread upon them; and let him never hold converse with a woman in her courses.

sanskrit: notsṛjeta purīṣaṃ ca kṣetre grāmasya cāntike ubhe mūtrapurīṣe tu nāpsu kuryāt kadā cana
english: Let him not void his dung in a field or near a village; and let him never pass either urine or dung into water.

sanskrit: prāṅmukho nityam aśnīyād vāgyato 'nnam akutsayan praskandayec ca manasā bhuktvā cāgnim upaspṛśet
english: Let him always eat facing the east, with curbed speech, not disparaging the food; let him offer it in mind, and when he has eaten, let him touch the fire.

sanskrit: āyuṣyaṃ prāṅmukho bhuṅkte yaśasyaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ dhanyaṃ paścānmukho bhuṅkte ṛtaṃ bhuṅkte udaṅmukhaḥ
english: Facing the east, he eats what brings long life; facing the south, what brings renown; facing the west, what brings wealth; facing the north, he eats in accord with truth.

sanskrit: nādhitiṣṭhet tuṣāñ jātu keśabhasmakapālikāḥ anyasya cāpy upasthānaṃ dūrataḥ parivarjayet
english: Let him never tread upon husks of grain, upon hair, ashes, or potsherds; and let him keep far away from the latrine of another.

sanskrit: śāntihomāṃś ca kurvīta sāvitrāṇi ca kārayet niṣaṇṇaś cāpi khādeta na tu gacchan kathaṃ cana
english: Let him perform the oblations for peace and have the Sāvitrī rites carried out; and let him eat while seated, never in any wise while walking.

sanskrit: mūtraṃ na tiṣṭhatā kāryaṃ na bhasmani na govraje
english: Urine should not be passed while standing, nor upon ashes, nor in a cattle-pen.

sanskrit: ārdrapādas tu bhuñjīta nārdrapādas tu saṃviśet ārdrapādas tu bhuñjāno varṣāṇāṃ jīvate śatam
english: Let him eat with feet wetted, but not lie down with feet wet; eating with feet wetted, he lives a hundred years.

sanskrit: trīṇi tejāṃsi nocchiṣṭa ālabheta kadā cana agniṃ gāṃ brāhmaṇaṃ caiva tathāsyāyur na riṣyate
english: Let him never, while unclean from leavings, touch the three sources of splendor — the fire, the cow, and the brāhmaṇa — and thus his life will not be diminished.
